To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the introduction of fluoroalkoxy substituent in the artemisinin scaffold can induce great changes on the permeation properties of the compounds, and the introduction of a hydroxyethylpiperazine substituent can increase the aqueous solution.
the introduction of fluorinated substituents in artemisinin and DHA ethers can lead to compounds with improved aqueous solubilities and, consequently, with better bioavailabilities.

the introduction of fluoroalkyloxy or trifluoromethyl group at the α‐methylenic carbon of DHA does not constitute an obstruction for artemisinin and F2DHA absorption after oral administration but does constitute an obstacle for F1‐DHa.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the permeation of fluorinated derivatives of artemisinin across the intestinal mucosal membrane.
the permeation of fluoroalkyldihydroartemisins across the rat intestine, and it provides useful information about the oral bioavailability of these compounds.
the development of new fluorinated derivatives of DHA with improved pharmacokinetics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the introduction of fluorinated groups into artemisinin and its derivatives does not constitute an absolute obstacle for the absorption of these compounds.

the introduction of fluoroalkoxy substituents in the DHA molecule does not affect the permeability of the molecule across the rat intestine, but the introduction of a trifluoromethyl group in the DHA scaffold decreases permeability.
the substitution of hydrogen atom by fluorine in the DHA scaffold is a good strategy for prolonging the half‐life, but it may be an obstacle for absorption after oral administration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introduction of fluorinated substituents at the 10β‐position of DHA ethers, which are known to be more active than the parent DHA, is an obstacle for the oral absorption of these compounds.
the introduction of fluorine atoms at the α‐carbon of the DHA ethers in the artemisinin molecule is not a promising strategy for improving the oral bioavailability.

the introduction of fluoroalkoxy substituent at the 10‐position of dihydroartesunate (10α‐(trifloropropyloxy)‐10,11‐dihydroartesunate) is a promising strategy to improve the aqueous soluibility and oral bioavailability of the compound.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the permeation of fluorinated analogs of artemisinin is highly dependent on the position of the fluoroalkyl substituent.
the introduction of fluoroalkyloxy groups into artemisinin derivatives may have a significant influence on their absorption and bioavailability.
fluorinated analogues of DHA may be good candidates for oral administration.
